summary: At least fourteen people died and eighteen were injured, five critically, after a chartered tour bus carrying at least 31 passengers from Mohegan Sun to the village of Uncasville crashed on Interstate 95 in The Bronx at about 0535 EST on Sunday. Driver Ophadell Williams, 40, told police the bus came into contact with a semi-trailer truck veering across the interstate, and that he swerved, overturned, scraped a railing for one hundred yards and struck a highway sign's upholding bar; Captain James Ellson described the scene as "a pile of humans, either still in their seats or on the floor, wrapped in the metal" and survivor Jose Hernandez said rescuers were hindered by twisted metal. The semi-trailer truck driver failed to stop and police are attempting to locate him; New York City Police Commissioner Raymond Kelly said the truck was moving on a lane to the bus' nearside, that whether the vehicles contacted each other is unconfirmed, and that both vehicles were travelling at "a significant rate of speed."
